newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower after hitting new record.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower after hitting new record.

text.p: Sustained profit taking in heavyweights such as Telkom and Gudang Garam pushed down the Jakarta share index on Thursday after it climbed to a new record, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.13 points, or 0.17 percent, to close at 684.98 points after touching a new high of 688.48 points earlier. However, in broader market sentiment, gainers led losers by 82 to 48, with 55 counters unchanged.
Total volume was 373.21 million shares on a turnover of 731.60 billion rupiah.
An analyst with a Hongkong-based securities firm said the market was likely to move in tight-range on Friday.

Psychologically the market will try to maintain the upward level after surpassing the previous record," she said. But added that the Jakarta index would be sensitive to Telkom's price in New York which had a 18.22 percent weighting on the index.
"Overall, there is some potential for the index to make slight gains," a local broker said.
Brokers said Bank Negara Indonesia might continue to lead market activity and help lift the index on Friday as interest on the stock remained strong.
Bank Negara topped the active list on the regular board with 84.3 million shares changing hands. It rose 125 rupiah to close at 1,700 rupiah after touching a high of 1,725 rupiah.

It cross-traded at a price of 1,675 rupiah on a volume of 4.7 million shares. Buying, especially in afternoon, was boosted in part by news that Standard & Poor gave the bank's $145 million notes issue a BBB long-term rating, brokers said.
Brokers also attributed the bank's gains to continued expectations of higher 1996 earnings, coupled with talk of its possible inclusion in Morgan Stanley's capital index.
Profit taking in toll road operator Citra Marga, cigarette makers Gudang Garam and Sampoerna weighed on the index.

Noodle maker Indofood rose 225 rupiah to 5,150 rupiah on a volume of 1.9 millon shares. "It was a target of foreign buyers. I also heard it might acquire a company," a foreign broker said. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Medium-sized Lippo Securities and fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudera were among stocks that made significant gains.
Brokerage Lippo Securities of the Lippo Group rose 10.11 percent to 2,450 rupiah on a turnover of 7.8 million shares on expectations of a better 1996 net profit, brokers said.
